title: Decision (spike): the did_webvh record as an app_data_dictionary component - update semantics, listing, external Commits
description:
Spike mimid-1wgh.4.81.32. draft-atwood-mls-didwebvh-credential-01 defines the record only as a GroupContext extension set by GroupContextExtensions; Open Issue 1/5 ask about carrying it as an app_data_dictionary component (mls-extensions-11 §4.6, §4.7). The draft defines no component semantics, so the prototype invents them (INVENTED, NOT FROM SPEC, behind CodePoints::with_heads_component; the GCE form stays the default).

Readings for the AppDataUpdate 'update' field: (a) the complete new DIDWebVHHeads, last update wins (as mls-extensions-11 §5.1 does for its built-ins); (b) a DIDWebVHHeads whose entries replace or add the entries of the same SCIDs, applied in Commit order (upsert); (c) one DIDWebVHHead per update. Chosen: (b). It reuses the record's struct and codec, a full record is also a valid update, and updates from several proposers (a device's by-reference partial update and the committer's) compose instead of the later one discarding the earlier. Entries are never removed, so upsert loses nothing the draft keeps. A remove op is invalid (the record MUST NOT be removed).

Other choices: mimi-mls is the component's application logic (like the §5.1 built-ins), so callers' apply functions never see it. The committer sends the whole expected record. Instead of required_capabilities, the GroupContext app_components list names the component (mls-extensions-11 §5: state may exist only for a listed component, and every member must list it); the first Commit that sets the record also extends app_components by AppDataUpdate. No required_capabilities is written. An external Commit may carry the record update (mls-extensions-11 §4.7 allows AppDataUpdate in external Commits), so a device or user newer than the record can join externally; this departs from the draft's §Rules, which is Open Issue 1.
